text: Lesson 10 showed that a health factor falls automatically as collateral's price drops. Liquidation is what happens the instant that number crosses below 1.0 — a threshold that makes a position eligible for anyone to act on.
A 1 ETH position starts with a health factor of 1.60 — safe. ETH drops to 1,200. The same formula gives 0.96 — below 1.0, eligible for liquidation, with no new action from the borrower at all.

A liquidator isn't the protocol team — it's any address, usually a bot, that calls the public liquidate function. Repay 500 dollars of debt and seize 525 dollars of collateral; the 5 percent difference is the liquidation bonus.

Any address can call liquidate the moment a position crosses the threshold. Bots monitor every position continuously and race for the bonus, and that competition is what keeps the system solvent — slow liquidations would let bad debt pile up.
A price move, a threshold crossed, a bot racing to profit from the difference. Next up: flash loans, the tool liquidators and arbitrageurs use to act without tying up their own capital.
